free_tier.stated: No free tier is stated; the vendor offers free trials for some plans through customer service, without naming the plans. A whole C-class range is priced per month by region: United States USD 500 at 100 Mbps; Spain, Netherlands, Australia, Brazil, Canada, United Kingdom, France and Germany USD 700 at 100 Mbps; Japan and Italy USD 750; Indonesia and India USD 800; Hong Kong and Vietnam USD 850; Dubai USD 900 at 50 Mbps; Taiwan, Malaysia and Thailand USD 950 at 100 Mbps and the Philippines USD 950 at 50 Mbps; Mexico USD 1,000 at 50 Mbps; South Korea USD 1,100 at 50 Mbps; Singapore USD 1,100 at 100 Mbps. That is USD 1.95 per address per month in the United States. The single static ISP product is USD 2.80 per IP for 30 days in the United States.
free_tier.notes: Prices are per range per month, not per byte: nothing on the page is a free allowance. A whole C-class range is a /24, 256 addresses, which is what makes USD 500 a month and USD 1.95 per address per month the same number in the United States.

per_object_cap.notes: An address block carries no stored object and therefore no per-object ceiling. The nearest structural cap is the block size itself: one /24, not a larger prefix.

retention.stated: not applicable: a leased address block, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The range is priced per month and delivered within one week after purchase; longer durations are arranged through online support. The single static ISP product offers validity periods of 7, 30 and 90 days. No minimum lease, renewal or reclaim term is stated for the range.

interface_detail: The range product's page states HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5, with other protocols on request to customer service. The range is delivered whole, 完整 IP 网段独立交付, within one week after purchase. The schema's interface enum has no proxy-protocol token, so the array keeps unknown and the protocols are stated here.
tooling: Proxy access over HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5, which the range product's page states; any client that takes a proxy address with credentials works: curl --proxy, Python requests with proxies=, a headless browser's proxy settings. Orders are managed in a console at console.linkstatic.com. No test address is published for the range product; checking the announcing AS and registration class of a delivered range takes a RIPE or ARIN whois lookup and a looking glass.
chaining: The range is an egress-address supply for a Workers gateway or a crawler: 256 addresses from one prefix spread a request stream across distinct source addresses, but every one of them shares one announcing AS, one registration class and one lease, so it adds address count without adding failure domains.

limits.value: 100 Mbps listed with the price of each region's range (50 Mbps for Dubai, the Philippines, Mexico and South Korea); the page does not state whether the figure applies per address or to the whole range
none: 无并发流量上限 (no concurrent-traffic cap) and no byte cap stated at any price tier

limits_note: The range is sold whole: no smaller contiguous prefix than a /24 is offered. The vendor states no traffic or concurrency limits; longer durations and greater bandwidth are arranged through online support, and delivery is within one week after purchase.
binding_note: The named ceiling is the bandwidth listed with each range, 100 Mbps, or 50 Mbps in Dubai, the Philippines, Mexico and South Korea; it is the only throughput figure on the product, since no traffic or concurrency limit is stated. Whether it applies per address or to the whole range is not stated. Structurally, one contiguous prefix means one announcing AS and one registration class, so a prefix-level block or withdrawal takes all 256 addresses at once.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up asks for an email address and a password of 8-22 characters with upper and lower case letters and numbers, plus an optional invitation code and a click-sequence verification code; Google sign-in is offered. No phone number and no identity document is asked. Payment methods at checkout: Alipay (two entries), cryptocurrency and account balance.

reliability_note: Bandwidth is listed per range, 100 Mbps or 50 Mbps, with no byte cap stated. No test address and no ASN is published for the range product, so the announcing AS and registration class cannot be checked before payment; the 256 addresses are one prefix, so a prefix-level blocklist entry or suspension removes all of them together. Paid services are non-refundable unless there is an IP quality issue.
confidence_note: Documented: the regional range prices and bandwidth figures, the protocol list, the free-trial and delivery terms, the payment methods and the sign-up fields are stated on the vendor's pricing and sign-up pages. Nothing about a delivered range is measured: measured needs one delivered or trial range, with an address checked against RIPE or ARIN whois for the registration class and a looking glass for the announcing AS.

price_per_tb_month: not applicable: priced per address per month, not per byte
notes: A whole C-class range is one contiguous /24 prefix: 256 addresses behind one announcing AS and one registration class, allocated whole to one customer. In the United States the range is USD 500 a month (a 30-day order line) at 100 Mbps, about USD 1.95 per address, and the range order total is the listed price times the number of ranges, with no quantity discount. The single static ISP product lists USD 2.80 per IP for 30 days in the United States, and its order total takes a quantity discount: 5 percent off for 1-5 IPs, 10 percent for 6-49, 15 percent for 50-199, 20 percent for 200-799 and 25 percent for 800 or more. 256 single addresses therefore come to USD 573.44 for 30 days (USD 716.80 at list price, less 20 percent), USD 2.24 per address, and the range costs about 13 percent less per address. No test address, no ASN and no prefix is published for the range product; the vendor offers free trials for some plans through customer service, and uses IPinfo as its reference for an address's region. A check of a delivered range takes a RIPE or ARIN whois lookup on one address for the registration class and a looking glass for the announcing AS.

extras.rung_note: One contiguous /24 is a single prefix: 256 addresses behind one announcing AS and one registration class, which is the rung-3 unit and the opposite of diversity.
extras.shaping: 100 Mbps listed per range (50 Mbps in Dubai, the Philippines, Mexico and South Korea); per address or per range is not stated; no byte cap
extras.quote: 完整 IP 网段独立交付，优化跨境传输体验，无并发流量上限
extras.quote_translation: a complete IP prefix delivered independently; cross-border transport optimised; no concurrent-traffic cap
extras.verification_gap: no test IP published for the block product, so the registration class and the announcing AS are unknown
extras.derivation: USD 1.95 per address per month is USD 500 / 256 = 1.953, rounded. 256 single static ISP addresses in the United States are 2.80 x 256 = 716.80 for 30 days at list price and 716.80 x 0.80 = 573.44 after the 20 percent discount for 200-799 IPs, 573.44 / 256 = 2.24 per address; the range is a 30-day order line at USD 500 with no quantity discount, and 500 / 573.44 = 0.872, about 13 percent less per address. These are arithmetic on stated prices, not measurements.
